title: Integrated Security & Compliance Policy - RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows & Risk Exceptions
author: Asha Patel
content:
Executive summary

This integrated policy consolidates Redwood Inference's controls and operational procedures across RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It is the canonical guidance for engineering, security, and GRC teams when designing, deploying, and operating services that handle customer or internal sensitive data.

Goals and scope
- Provide a single reference for security controls required by contract, regulation, and internal SLAs.
- Define ownership, SLOs, alert thresholds, and evidence collection steps to support audits.
- Cover both Redwood-hosted and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment modes.
- Audience: engineering, platform, SRE, security, compliance, and solutions engineering.

1) RBAC and Authentication
Introduction
Redwood enforces least-privilege access using a role-based access control (RBAC) model mapped to cloud IAM and an internal permissions service ("permsvc"). All human and machine identities must authenticate via SSO (OIDC/SAML) and be authorized by permsvc before accessing any control plane or data plane operations.

Key concepts and roles
- Roles: viewer, developer, operator, oncall, security-admin, infra-admin, compliance-auditor, customer-admin (for private deployments).
- Scopes: project/org, model, environment (dev/staging/prod), resource type (endpoint, dataset, key).
- Machine identities: short-lived workload identities (mTLS / KSA) used by services and CI.

Policy requirements
- Authentication: SSO enabled for all employees; MFA mandatory (TOTP or hardware).
- Authorization: role assignments must be recorded in permsvc. Production write operations require operator or higher.
- Privileged access: security-admin and infra-admin require quarterly attestation and approval by security.
- Temporary elevation: use Just-in-Time (JIT) access with time-bound grant and automated audit record.

Operational controls and checks
- Periodic review: org-level role reviews every 90 days; automated reminders and re-certification.
- Onboarding/offboarding: new accounts onboard via HR integration; offboard triggers immediate revocation.
- Enforcement: deny-by-default on all control plane APIs; permsvc denies requests lacking explicit allow rule.

Example: permission check (pseudocode)
- curl -X POST https://permsvc.internal/api/v1/check \n  -d '{"subject":"user:alice@example.com","action":"invoke","resource":"endpoint:model-prod-v1"}'

2) Audit Logging
Purpose
Audit logs provide tamper-evident records for access, configuration changes, and data movement to support investigations and audits. Logs are segregated into control-plane logs, data-plane access logs, and infrastructure logs.

Minimum logged fields
- timestamp, principal (user/service), action, resource, outcome (allow/deny), request id, region, host/service, correlation ids, reason (if provided).

Retention and storage
- Control-plane logs: retained 7 years for enterprise customers with contractual requirements; default retention 2 years for non-enterprise.
- Data-plane access logs (sensitive): 7 years for regulated customers; default 1 year.
- Immutable storage: logs are streamed to write-once object storage (WORM) and replicated across two regions for disaster recovery.

Integrity and monitoring
- Logs are hashed and signed weekly; hash roots stored in a dedicated integrity ledger.
- SIEM ingestion: Splunk/Chronicle receives control-plane and infra logs in near-real time.
- Alerting: anomalous access (e.g., mass data exports, multiple failed auths) generates P1/P2 alerts routed to security oncall.

Example logging configuration (YAML excerpt)
- audit: \n    enabled: true\
    sink: s3://redwood-logs/audit/{year}/{month}\
    format: json\
    retention_days: 3650  # enterprise override supported

3) Data Residency & Retention
Residency principles
- Customers choose region(s) for persistent data at provisioning time for Private and Dedicated offerings. Hosted API supports region routing by customer tier.
- Short-lived in-memory processing may occur outside residency region only when explicitly allowed in contract; such flows must use ephemeral encryption keys and be logged.

Retention policy matrix
- Customer configuration, model assets, and training data: retention per customer contract (default 3 years for backups; otherwise customer-configurable).
- Logs: as defined in Audit Logging.
- KV caches and ephemeral prompts: 30 days by default unless customer requests shorter retention or opt-out.

Data deletion and verification
- Self-serve deletion: API and Console provide data deletion workflows; deletions produce a deletion-job id and audit record.
- Proof of deletion: for sensitive datasets, the platform emits a signed deletion certificate (contains job id, resources deleted, and timestamp).
- Backup lifecycle: backups are rotated and zeroed according to retention schedule; deletion from backups may be delayed up to 48 hours to allow for in-progress operations - this window is documented in the deletion cert.

4) Secure SDLC (Software Development Lifecycle)
Requirements summary
- All code touching customer data or infrastructure must follow secure SDLC controls: threat modeling, dependency scanning, static analysis (SAST), dynamic testing (DAST for web components), secrets scanning, and PR-level security reviews.

Checkpoints and gating
- Design review: required for new services or major schema changes; must include threat model and data flow diagram.
- CI gates: PR cannot merge if SAST or dependency-scan fails; critical CVEs block merge until fixed or mitigated with documented exception.
- Pre-release: canary rollout with automated canary audits (latency, error rate, and data handling validation).

Developer tooling and recommended practices
- Use sandboxed feature branches with ephemeral credentials.
- Secrets management: all secrets must be in KMS-backed secret manager; no plaintext secrets in repos.
- Reproducible builds: build artifacts signed and reproducible; provenance recorded in release manifest.

5) Incident Response - Security Procedures
Objectives
- Contain, eradicate, recover, and notify stakeholders per severity and regulatory requirements.

Severity classification and SLAs
- Sev1 (P1): Customer-impacting data exfiltration or production control-plane compromise. SLA: ack in 15 minutes, incident leader oncall.
- Sev2 (P2): Partial service degradation or suspected unauthorized access. SLA: ack in 1 hour.
- Sev3 (P3): Non-urgent security findings. SLA: ack within 24 hours.

Runbook highlights
1. Triage: collect timeline, affected resources, initial indicators of compromise (IOCs), and impacted customers.
2. Containment: rotate credentials/keys, isolate compromised hosts (k8s cordon/drain), apply temporary ACLs.
3. Evidence preservation: snapshot affected instances, preserve audit and network logs, escalate to forensic team if necessary.
4. Root cause analysis: assign RCA owner; begin timeline and hypothesis-driven testing.
5. Recovery & validation: restore services from last-known-good artifacts and validate via smoke tests and canary.
6. Notification: follow legal and contractual notification timelines; security and legal coordinate customer communications.

Command examples
- kubectl cordon <node>
- aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id vol-012345 --description "incident-2027-03"

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Purpose
- Standardize how teams collect, store, and present evidence for audits (SOC2, ISO, customer audits).

Evidence catalog (examples)
- RBAC: role assignment exports, attestation logs, JIT access audit.
- Audit logging: signed log hashes, retention policy configs, SIEM alerts.
- SDLC: design review notes, SAST/DAST results, release manifests, signed artifacts.
- Incident response: incident timeline, containment steps, root cause analysis, remediation evidence.

Evidence collection process
1. Submit evidence request in the compliance tracker (Jira project: GRC-EVIDENCE).
2. Evidence owner (documented in page metadata) collects artifacts and uploads to evidence bucket with evidence-id.
3. Automation validates completeness (checksums, timestamps) and marks evidence as ready for review.
4. Reviewer approves or requests supplemental evidence; reviewed artifacts archived to immutable evidence store.

Retention and access
- Evidence stored in a restricted bucket with 2-person access control for deletion.
- Access logs for evidence retrieval recorded and retained per audit retention matrix.

7) Risk & Exceptions
Policy for exceptions
- Exceptions to controls are rare, timebound, and risk-assessed. Exception requests are submitted to the Risk & Exceptions board (quarterly review) via an Exceptions template.

Required fields for an exception request
- Owner, affected control(s), justification, compensating controls, timeline (start/end), rollback criteria, and acceptance criteria.

Approval process and tagging
- Minor exceptions (low-risk, <30 days) can be approved by security manager + product owner.
- Major exceptions (>30 days, high-risk) require board approval (security, compliance, engineering leadership, and legal).
- Approved exceptions must be tagged in permsvc and in asset inventory.

Monitoring and closure
- Exception owners must provide weekly progress updates and confirm compensating controls are effective. Exceptions auto-expire and are re-evaluated before renewal.

Appendices
A. Contacts and ownership
- Security team oncall: security-oncall@redwood.com
- Compliance (evidence requests): compliance-evidence@redwood.com
- Permsvc owners: infra-auth@redwood.com

B. SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)
- Auth failures anomaly: >1000 failed logins across accounts in 10 min -> P1 alert.
- Unusual data egress: flows >100GB from a single org in 30 min -> P1.
- Log pipeline lag: >5 min median ingest lag -> P2.

C. Related templates and artifacts
- Exception request template: /templates/exception-request.md
- Evidence upload manifest: /templates/evidence-manifest.json
- Threat model template: /templates/threat-model.md
